standard_prerequisites.name: Hypergraphs induced by arithmetic progressions
standard_prerequisites.statement: For sets D and M of natural numbers, the family A of subscript D M consists of the hypergraphs on a finite set S of natural numbers whose edges are the intersections of S with finite arithmetic progressions of difference in D and whose starting points satisfy the congruence condition M; the family with the superscript infinity uses infinite progressions instead; the author's own definition is retained at source lines 271-276.
standard_prerequisites.use: They are the two families whose thresholds the counted theorem bounds and studies, and the shorthand m of subscript D M is exactly what its statement writes.

standard_prerequisites.name: The parameter m_H(k) and its shorthand
standard_prerequisites.statement: The parameter m_H(k) is the smallest threshold admitting polychromatic k-colourings of every member after deleting the edges of size below the threshold, and the article writes m of subscript D M for the value on the family of arithmetic progressions; retained at source lines 128-129 and 278-280.
standard_prerequisites.use: The counted theorem asserts an upper bound and an infinitude for two such values, so both the parameter and the shorthand must be available.

standard_prerequisites.name: The family of axis-parallel rectangles as a comparison
standard_prerequisites.statement: The proof of the second item reduces to a three-dimensional family of translates of octants and compares it with the family induced by axis-parallel rectangles, whose threshold is infinite by a cited theorem recorded in the article's introduction; that entry is cited inside the counted proof and is supplied with this card as a fragment of the bibtex-formatted entry.
standard_prerequisites.use: The comparison with the rectangle family is what goes through to give the infinitude in the second item.

core_obligations: First item, first half: show that the threshold for differences the powers of t and the congruence condition M is at most the number of elements of M times the threshold of the bottomless-rectangle family minus one plus one, by constructing an injection from the natural numbers into the plane such that every initial segment of an arithmetic progression of difference t to the i is the trace of the image on a bottomless rectangle (source line 926).

Continue the injection argument: the vertical strip indexed by the endpoints of the progression contains the images of the numbers between them and the half plane below one over i contains the images of the multiples of t to the i, so the image of the progression is exactly the intersection of the image of the injection with one bottomless rectangle (source line 926).

Pass to the general congruence condition: place t bottomless rectangles so that the r-th one contains the images of the numbers congruent to r modulo t, and transport the previous computation to the injection that adds two r to the first coordinate, checking both the case where the first element of the progression is not congruent to r and the case where it is (source lines 928-930).

Finish the first item with the case of difference one: any edge with at least the number of elements of M times the bottomless threshold minus one plus one vertices contains, by the pigeonhole principle, at least the bottomless threshold many vertices inside one of the rectangles, and those numbers form an arithmetic progression of difference t, which the previous step already shows lies in a bottomless rectangle (source lines 932-933).

Second item, first step: define the three-dimensional family of translates of octants, and prove the nested lemma that its threshold is infinite by intersecting it with a plane whose normal vector is zero one one and whose coordinate axes are chosen so that every axis-parallel rectangle of the plane arises as the trace of a set of the family (source lines 937-943).

Second item, conclusion: compare the family of the counted theorem with the three-dimensional one by transporting the injection already built in the proof of the previous theorem, note that every hextant is contained in an octant and that the image of a hextant is a prefix of an arithmetic progression with the required divisibility, and conclude that the threshold is at least the infinite threshold of the three-dimensional family, hence infinite (source lines 953-959).

proof_roadmap.step: First item: build the injection and observe that progressions of fixed difference are traces on bottomless rectangles.
Generalise to a congruence condition by placing t bottomless rectangles side by side.
Close the first item by the pigeonhole argument for difference one.
Second item: define the octant family and prove the nested lemma giving its infinite threshold.
Transport the injection and conclude infinitude.

difficulty_reason: 计数单元是 arXiv:2307.12154v3 的 Theorem veges_sorozat（源 346-359 行，两段证明分别在 925-934 与 936-960 行）：(1) 若 M 在每个模 t 剩余类中至多取一个元素，则差集为 t 的幂、起始点受限的算术级数超图族的阈值不超过 |M|(m_B(k)−1)+1；(2) 对互素的 p、q，差集为 p^i q^j 时阈值为无穷。关键操作不是例行核验：第一段要造一个把自然数嵌入平面的单射 φ，使「固定差 t^i 的级数初段」恰好等于像集与某个底矩形的交（926 行），再为一般剩余类条件并排放 t 个底矩形并把计算搬过去（928-930 行），最后用鸽笼把「任意一条大边必含某矩形内的 m_B(k) 个点」接上（932-933 行）；第二段要先定义三维八分体族并用一个法向量为 (0,1,1) 的平面把它与平面矩形族对上，证出嵌套引理（阈值无穷，937-943 行），再用已有单射把两类超图对应起来收尾（953-959 行）。难点在于两段都用「几何族与数列族之间的保边对应」这一手法，且第一段的单射必须同时处理差为 t^i 与差为 1 两种情形；原文位置在证明的 926、928-930、932-933 与 937-943 行。
